newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher as LME spread surges.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher as LME spread surges.

text.p: COMEX copper settled sharply higher as spreads flared on LME due to covering of tight dates in April and May, and concerns over near term supplies, traders said.
May COMEX copper settled 2.70 cents firmer at 109.90 cents per pound, traded 111.00 to 107.40 cents. Spot April went out 3.10 cents firmer at 110.50 cents. Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots.
"The reality is the market had a good demand structure and it took a little technical push to get things going," Bill O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said.

Copper futures exploded through key, upside chart levels to trigger stop loss covering against a background of maintenance shutdown at Kennecott's smelter, forthcoming labor talks at Phelps Dodge's Chino mine, and the continuing strike at Escondida mine in Chile, the world's biggest.
LME stocks also fell 1,875 tonnes Tuesday to 150,125 tonnes as inventory continues to fall from already low levels.
There was talk that Canadian copper trader Herbert Black was one of the influential shorts being squeezed. Black said he was out of the market and has no short or long position.
The LME cash to three months backwardation surged to $105/$115, up from about $60 on Monday when the spread began to strengthen, an early indication of what was to come, traders said.
The market's closing provides a good technical footing, and a big fund short commitment in the market belies the strong offtake of red metal, O'Neill said.
